status: Proposed damage-state review geometry; the committed guide remains the clean ship
units: Vanilla hull-space units (1 sprite px = 1 unit); multiply by metres_per_unit for metres
revision: V3 detail: segmented sprite-measured hull, whole engine pods, spine command deck, port grapple, naval turrets

thickness_profile.method: Flat deck plateaus (x0, x1, deck z) over single-chamfer sections; level keel

port_fitting.function: Proposed boarding/cargo grapple sponson and folded arm, read from the sprite; not canonical lore

mesh_authority: All views render the same objects; generated surface art is subordinate to this geometry.

scars.note: Unpowered for the years in the belt; lit from the escape on.
Continuity scar 1: canon puts a rough patch under the collar at arrival; the refit sorted the forward collar out with a proper plate.
On the cheek facet above the sponson, over occupied space: a welded doubler for the flight; untouched by the refit; re-plated in the restoration. Sized to the facet.
Not needed for the flight; re-plated only in the restoration.
Not needed for the flight; re-plated only in the restoration.
Lee knock; cosmetic, painted over.
Lee knock; cosmetic, painted over.
Lee knock; cosmetic, painted over.
The slow knock that bowed the jamb and jammed the door: a crease, not a hole; faired and painted once the door was freed.
Continuity scar 1: small strikes round the sponson; left open, painted over when restored.
Windward deck; outside the pressure hull, left open.
Only strikes over the command deck got pressure patches.
Armour only, not pressure: left; re-plated when restored.
Armour only: left; re-plated when restored.
Armour only, on the chine: left; built up with weld and dressed, painted over when restored (a plate cannot lie flat across the chine).
Armour only: left; re-plated when restored.
A rock rolled along the sponson; cosmetic, painted over.
Glancing contact across plate seams; painted over.
Torn by a strike; deck armour, not flight-critical; plated in the refit over the new berthing.
Torn by a strike; replaced when restored.
Unbolted by salvagers; a proper plate fitted in the refit.
Slow heavy contact; left buckled for the escape, cut out and re-plated in the refit.
Where the hulk was moored; nobody needed it gone until the restoration ground it flush.
Bowed by the bay-door knock; shored for the flight; a new section welded in when restored.
Jammed; welded shut for pressure and thrust loads; freed when the jamb was rebuilt.
Coil lifted and feeds cut in the belt; blind-flanged and left cold for the escape and the refit; restored with a new coil.
Coil lifted in the belt; the escape ran on a salvaged coil and a jury feed; restored to the pod as built.
Turbopumps taken off the port housing deck; reinstalled at restoration.
Turbopumps taken off the starboard deck; the jury coil and feed pump stood in for them until restoration.
Port can feed pipes cut out for their metal; renewed at restoration.
Both pods' outboard access panels carried off; never needed for the flight.
Engine 1 can stove in and torn, bell mouth crushed out of round, top ram snapped, collar torn: crushed against the anchor rock; a new can and nozzle at restoration.

The rock that crushed Engine 1 stove in the upper outboard quarter of the whole port engine bay: barrel bands and fin cage pressed flat (five fin rings crushed together, the cage rail bent in and torn), the thrust housing corner knocked in, one panel torn off and folded back and another gone over a void with broken frames and feed runs cut toward the can. Absorbs the old bent-fins row. The pod is cold, so it stays as it is until the bay is rebuilt with the new can.
Heaviest strike on the ship, over the dead pod; never plated, painted over.
Windward strike low on the port casing.
Windward strike on the port intake cap.
Lee-side slow knock: a shallow lipless dent.
Small strikes round the shoulder crater.
Small strikes on the port pod flank.
Rock rolled along the port pod as the hulk swung.
Glancing gouge across the port cowl top.
Unbolted by salvagers off the cold pod; plated only at restoration.
Unbolted by salvagers; salvage sheet over the running pod for the escape, a proper plate at the refit.
Casing plate buckled by slow contact; renewed at restoration.
The aft mooring point; tether cut at the shackle for the escape; ground off at restoration.
A fast dorsal strike on the port armour plate beside the plant well. Not pressure or thrust: left open through the escape and the refit; painted over as a shallow dent once restored.
Small dorsal strikes across the engine-room roof; the armour took them, nothing was breached, so nobody patched them until the restoration paint.
Starboard (lee) armour plate unbolted by salvagers, not torn: a clean stud ring. Left bare for the flight; an easy proper plate in the refit.

Power from the starboard jury coil to the cold engine room, run outside and clipped down for thrust; still in service through the limited refit, gone once restored (internal feed, hatch blank removed).
A fast strike from port-above on the port prong armour block over the cradle winch. Tow-cradle machinery: nothing the flight or the refit needed.
A slow tumbling contact that dragged inboard along the top of the stern cross girder from its port end, shearing bolt heads. Cosmetic: painted over.
Strike on the spine housing over occupied space: welded doubler in the escape, plated properly by the berthing conversion.
Small strikes along the spine and command deck: pressure patches, then inserts.
Scattered deck strikes; only those over the occupied spine are ever patched.
Hatch seal taken; borrowed gasket; proper seal fitted in the conversion.
Hatch seal taken; borrowed gasket; proper seal fitted in the conversion.
Hatch seal taken; borrowed gasket; proper seal fitted in the conversion.
Seal and hinge taken; dogged shut under a bolted blank; reopened on a new hinge as the berthing's second exit.
Mast sheared above the pedestal; jury whip and salvaged nav sensor for the flight; the command conversion fits a proper flanged upper section and scanner.

Drift strike bent the barrel at the chase and slewed the house 24 deg aft until the traverse seized, so it would not lift off: left as scrap, flown dead and jammed; new house on an adapter ring in restoration.
Gun house stripped; a gantry house from another hull bolted back in its owner's primer; repainted to near match.

House holed through the roof and the barrel snapped on the chase: left as scrap. Its feed, torn inside the hole, went live when the crew powered the mount bus (sparks); isolated and booted in the conversion; new house in restoration.
Gun house stripped; its own house recovered from the gantry and reinstalled on an adapter ring; ring painted over.
Protected waist line cut for its contents: sleeved for the flight, spooled in restoration.
Exposed waist trunk feeds the spine: the command conversion re-runs it with a new spool.
Dead while unpowered; working as built from the escape on.
stbd bell taken in the belt; refitted from salvage for the escape, reinstalled as built at restoration.
All four bells stripped; the escape refitted salvaged up and down bells for the roll couple, port and fore stay blanked until restored.
Dead while unpowered; working as built from the escape on.

Whole block unbolted off the port thrust housing; its feed blind-flanged for the escape. Not needed while the port pod is cold (the starboard drive already yaws the bow to port); reinstalled at restoration.
Dead while unpowered; working as built from the escape on.
up-2 taken in the belt and blanked for the escape; a new bell fitted at the refit.
Dead while unpowered; working as built from the escape on.

Windward port waist deck: a tumbling rock tore five deck panels away along their seams, folding one back over the deck and breaking the frame under the strike; the waist service runs broke in the void. Not pressure, thrust or navigation: left open through the escape (the bus conduit arcing where nobody could reach it in vacuum); the refit ran the new berthing services through it and plated it; painted when restored.

Starboard waist deck: four panels torn off in the same tumble, one folded back over the inboard seam, a coolant line crushed and the starboard bus conduit severed. Left open for the escape (arcing); the refit ran the new berthing services through this void and closed it with a proper plate.

Forward deck over the command deck's forward end: deck armour panels torn off down to the frames, one folded back along its seam. Over occupied space, so the escape crew welded a salvage pressure plate across it, strongbacked, the torn surround and the folded panel left as they were; a proper plate in the refit.

Port forebody outboard deck: a glancing contact along the deck edge caught one long deck plate at its forward end and rolled it back up and over along its outboard seam, the cable tray beneath torn. Outside the pressure hull: left; re-plated when restored.

Starboard forebody outboard deck: the same tumble dragged along the starboard deck edge and rolled one long deck plate up and outboard on its seam, a conduit run snapped beneath. Outside the pressure hull: left; re-plated when restored.
